flume.pageTitle: Beluga vs Flume: Non-Invasive Water Monitor Comparison
flume.metaDescription: Compare Beluga and Flume — two non-invasive water monitors for different environments. Residential usage tracking vs commercial water intelligence. Neutral comparison.
flume.heroSubtitle: Both are non-invasive water monitors — but they are built for very different environments and levels of depth.
flume.introP1: If you are searching for a Flume alternative or comparing non-invasive water monitoring options, it is worth understanding that non-invasive installation does not mean identical capability. Beluga and Flume are both non-invasive, but they are designed for different audiences, different scales, and different levels of system insight.
flume.introP2: This page compares the two based on publicly available information to help you determine which fits your situation.
flume.midTitle: Non-invasive, but built for different environments
flume.midSubtitle: The shared non-invasive approach may suggest these products are interchangeable, but the target environment and analytical depth are quite different.
flume.midLeftP: Flume provides non-invasive water monitoring for homeowners, focusing on tracking daily usage, setting budgets, and detecting unusual activity. It is designed to clamp onto a residential water meter and deliver clear, simple insights through a consumer-friendly app.
flume.midRightP: Beluga extends the non-invasive concept into commercial-grade system intelligence. It monitors entire building water systems, identifies individual fixtures through pattern recognition, detects inefficiencies, and provides long-term behavioral analysis beyond aggregate usage tracking.

faq.q: Are Beluga and Flume installed the same way?
faq.a: Both emphasize non-invasive installation. Specific hardware placement and sensor type may differ. Beluga is designed for commercial plumbing systems, while Flume is designed for residential water meters.

faq.q: Is Flume good for commercial buildings?
faq.a: Flume is primarily designed and marketed for residential, single-family homes. Commercial and multi-unit applications are not its core focus based on publicly available information.

Beluga is primarily oriented toward commercial buildings, multi-unit properties, and building operators. Homeowners looking for simple usage tracking may find Flume or similar residential products more relevant.

faq.q: What makes Beluga different from Flume if both are non-invasive?
faq.a: While both are non-invasive, they serve different markets and offer different depth. Flume tracks household water usage and alerts to anomalies. Beluga builds a behavioral model of an entire building's water system, identifies individual fixtures, and provides intelligence beyond aggregate usage.

faq.q: Can I use Flume to monitor a multi-unit building?
faq.a: Flume is designed for individual residential water meters. Multi-unit or commercial water systems are outside its typical deployment scope. Beluga is built for these types of environments.
